automation_control.coverage: Showcase only: 2 exact pipeline goals plus one registered two-buffer template; separate from the 61 benchmark queries.
automation_control.interpretation: Ordinary Lean automation solves the showcase without discovered lemmas when this control succeeds. This is counterevidence to broad proving-superiority claims; resources differ from restricted graph search.
automation_control.method: Lean grind (gen := 32) after unfolding registered stage definitions

formal_verification.scope: All candidate proofs and successful baseline/one-canonical-selection witnesses in every training/validation context; every distinct successful baseline/augmented test witness across all policies and random repetitions. Training single-candidate label searches are not individually certified. Failed searches produce no theorem.
formal_verification.timing_interpretation: Elapsed seconds is actual certification wall time. Summed subprocess elapsed seconds adds overlapping process wall times; neither is a measured CPU-time counter.

holdout_audit.scope: Recognized statement equality under the registered sound partial normalizer; no claim of deciding all mathematical equivalences.

limitations: All consequences are globally known nonexpansive list-length compositions; no mathematical originality claim.
Registry omission creates search difficulty; it does not create a difficult mathematical theorem.
Operator-skeleton shift only, not mathematical-domain or graph-generator-family transfer.
Typed symbolic hashes are conventional feature hashing, not pretrained semantic embeddings.
Historical reuse is operator-motif frequency in generated training proofs, not Mathlib chronology or human citations.
Conservative normalization excludes recognized equivalent goals and restatements; unrecognized mathematical equivalences may remain.

Label-free theorem-statement cleaning can leave empty goal contexts, and equivalence filtering can leave sparse or empty candidate pools. Empty contexts remain in context averages with zero solved-goal contribution; actual retained query counts determine goal denominators.

When a context has at most three eligible candidates every policy supplies the entire pool, so it provides no selected-set ranking comparison. Count contexts with a genuine ranking choice before interpreting model differences.
Ensemble disagreement is not calibrated epistemic uncertainty.
A bounded graph-search failure is not proof that a candidate is mathematically necessary.
The stronger general Lean automation control covers the showcase only, with different resources and foundational axioms; no full-benchmark tactic superiority claim.

model_history.interpretation: Operator-motif reuse, not Mathlib history or human theorem citations.
model_history.source: successful frozen training baseline proof-search witnesses only

model_training.embedding: 16-dimensional normalized signed SHA-256 hash of typed operator syntax; not pretrained
model_training.history: operator motifs of successful frozen training baseline proof witnesses only
model_training.label: one-lemma marginal bounded downstream solve fraction

normalization_rules.scope: Generic shared-predicate/k equality-law provenance; this file does not certify the Python normalizer as a complete equivalence procedure.

protocol.budget_accounting: At most three selected lemmas (or the whole eligible pool when smaller) and at most eight dequeued BFS propositions per goal, every method. Every policy has identical selected count within each context. Primitive proof edges and concrete list-operation counts reported separately. Training, candidate enumeration, and kernel certification are additional costs. No matched wall-time or Lean tactic budget claim.
protocol.candidate_normalization: Normalize with registered shared-predicate/k laws: filter idempotence on known-passing elements, redundant take on known-within-k lists, reverse cancellation and commuting rules, plus length-preserving outer map/reverse and repeated same-k minima. Exclude normalized identity, known-edge/seed, equivalent held-out-goal and duplicate pairs; keep the cheapest surviving witness for every policy. This is not a complete theorem-equivalence oracle.
protocol.endpoint_visibility: Unlabelled test goal endpoints visible to all task-conditioned rankers; no held-out outcomes or proof paths in model features.
protocol.goal_rule: Start with the deterministic 20 endpoint pairs per context at minimum stage-index span six. Before any fitting or solve outcomes, prune identity, own-primitive/seed-equivalent statements, and within-context normalized duplicates. Train on retained training goals. Remove validation goals seen in any training primitive/seed/retained-goal/candidate declaration; remove test goals seen in that training index or any validation primitive/seed/retained-goal/candidate declaration. Do not refill, resample, or drop empty contexts. Denominators are actual retained query counts.
protocol.holdout: Distinct operator skeleton families and frozen seeds only. Every split uses the same procedural DAG topology generator and the same List Nat mathematical domain; this is not graph-family or mathematical-domain transfer.
protocol.label: Measured one-candidate marginal goal-solve fraction, including zero and negative outcomes, training contexts only.
leakage_controls: Distinct split seed ranges and context hashes
No exact evaluation-goal pair offered as a candidate
Operator skeleton families disjoint by construction
Same frozen candidate pool and k/BFS budget for all policies
Structure-only ablation trained on identical natural training graphs
Reuse motif history frozen from successful training baseline witnesses
protocol.rejected_predecessors: Attempt1 was rejected for equivalent-goal leakage and a length-identity seed. Attempt2 was rejected because 46/240 test endpoint queries matched recognized training declarations (10 training-goal and 36 primitive-edge occurrences), despite valid kernel proofs. Both attempts and diagnostics are preserved. This run applies label-free prior-statement pruning and retrains without changing generator sizes, operator families or hyperparameters to obtain utility gains.
protocol.seed_constraint: Choose the nearest two-edge chain window containing filter/take whose endpoints have different strong length-normal-form keys, before goals or labels. A syntactically reducing operation alone is insufficient because shared-predicate/k identities can make it redundant.
protocol.verification: Independent fresh Lean processes certify actual List Nat propositions with a propext-only allowlist when certify=True. Graph search alone is not proof.
